column1: # The FFI bench gate record: one line per check, the target it runs on, the
# .tono it compiles, and the outcome scripts/check-ffi-bench.sh must observe.
# A check that ends elsewhere than recorded fails the gate, in both
# directions: a regression on a green row, and a red row that starts passing
# (update this record and README.md together, that is the progress report).
# outcome: pass | frontend-red | gen-red | build-red | test-red | run-red | refused
# 02: the per-language name itself resolves (ConstantCalculator<f64>); the
# red is the narrower gap left behind: compute is a trait method on the
# concretely held type and nothing brings the trait into scope.
# 07: the handle resolves behind the trait now; the red is the struct
# literal (the foreign options struct's own name and the Some(..) wrap).
# 11: the call's receiver is the foreign type itself (FormulaCalculator.parse);
# Go has no static method, so its row passes by being refused at generation.
# 12: the call passes a declared handle's class itself (instantiate(AnswerCalculator));
# Rust and Go have no type as a value, so their rows pass by being refused.
# 13: the call passes a map literal ({ "answer": .answer, "other": 1.5 }) for a
# map[string]float parameter; every target has a string-keyed map to spell it as.
